title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 16
paragraphs: While Xerxes's forces were sailing in formation toward them, the Greeks stayed quiet at Artemisium; and the barbarians, having formed their ships into a crescent to enclose them, were trying to surround them. Then the Greeks put out and engaged; and in this battle the two sides were nearly equal. For Xerxes's fleet, by its great size and numbers, suffered damage from itself, as ships were thrown into confusion and crashed into one another; yet it held its ground and did not give way, disdaining to be turned to flight by so few ships. Many Greek ships were destroyed and many men perished, but far more of the barbarians' ships and men. So, having fought in this manner, they parted and each returned to his own station.
